body: Can you explain why did you need this new dependency?
I just try to stay close as much as possible to the RIS markup.
Why do we have min > max here? Is it to trigger the disabled state? Shouldn't it be an error to have max > min in the options of the widget factory?

I was a bit surprised with this default value. When using the arrows to increase / decrease the value, using a step of .01 is a bit slow. But since the step adds a validation rule on the input it's a tricky choice. (I don't have a good solution here)

Not sure that we should impose a validation on the `min` and `max`. Is it unreasonable that we want to use a wider range? Or maybe that solves some techical related problems? Happy to hear about your insights here :)
Nice move 👍 Let's deprecate all the things! (in the limits of the usability of the library 🤣 )
Maybe for the sake of readability we could rename range into currentRange?
Maybe for the sake of readability we could rename range into currentRange?
Couldn't we rely on snapshots here? I'm not sure that relying on mocks helps much or does it?

I tried to keep the same behaviour in the `RangeInput` & `RangeSlider`. In the later if the given `min` value is higher or equal than `max` the slider is disabled.

But we can definitely throw an error in the `RangeInput`, and do the same in the `RangeSlider` in the next major release.
Yes you are right, it's a bit slow! We can provide `0` as default value to enable only integer.

I think we should validate it, because the `min` & `max` are the range where the user is able to search. It doesn't make sense to let it put an higher or lower. IMO we need to show a hint (in this case the `HTML5` validation) to the user that his search is out of bounds and so irrelevant.

With the actual implementation one thing that it might happen if we don't set the limit on the input is this:

* the user set the input out of bounds
* the user submit the form
* the search will be trigger with original values
* the render method will erase your current out of bounds values and replaced with the actual state

One thing that we could do is to be more precise when we refine. Currently, we just check that [one of the values has changed](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/develop/src/connectors/range-slider/connectRangeSlider.js#L134) if its the case we clear the refinements. Then we set the refinement **IF** [the value are correct](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/develop/src/connectors/range-slider/connectRangeSlider.js#L142). But the search & render will be trigger [even if the value is not set](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/develop/src/connectors/range-slider/connectRangeSlider.js#L162). A solution could be to handle the values separately, in this way we could pass a falsy value without triggering the search & render.

WDYT?
I mock the render method in order to be able to use the snapshot on it.
0 should be fine. They can customize it.
